Visit note | 2026-04-29 11:00 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Fariha Matubbar, 55, female. Mrs. Matubbar returns for review regarding persistent soreness and itching in her intimate area, noting that these episodes have been returning four times a year. She is a software developer and states the problem started after a course of antibiotics taken in Rampura. She mentions her symptoms recur despite home care. She has Essential hypertension. She denies fever, pelvic pain, or abnormal discharge. Examination reveals random blood glucose 5.4 mmol/L, BP 142/89 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, and weight 60 kg. External examination shows localized erythema without significant skin breakdown. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued today. She was advised to wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.
